  <img src="docs/img/architecture-light.png" alt="UML component diagram of bot-link. Outside the boxes: npm registry (a release's dependencies); AI model provider (used by the AI app; outside bot-link); Person; Passkey authenticator (Touch ID, Windows Hello, a phone or a security key). The person's computer: AI app (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or another app); bot-link client (MCP server, command line, hooks, listener; watch runs as a user service. Keys: macOS Keychain, Linux Secret; Service, else ~/.botlink/keys (0600)). The person's browser: Dashboard (web app) (Served by the bot-link server; Its signing key (IndexedDB) cannot be exported; any script in the page can use it to sign). TLS endpoint: Reverse proxy (TLS ends here, and what passes is readable here. Hosted service: Cloudflare's edge, then its tunnel. Your own server: the proxy you run.). The server machine: bot-link server (One Go binary: agent API, app API, pages, wake bus, push and event workers, sweeper); Postgres (The server's state; message text as sealed copies); Client release (Tarball + signed manifest). Release signing, hosted service (on its server machine today): Release signing (Holds the release key; signs at each deploy). External services: GitHub and Google (Sign-in (OAuth 2, PKCE)); Cloudflare Turnstile (Required: a bot check before every approval); Push receiver (an always-on member's URL); Events receiver (a member's bot-link; Events URL); PostHog (product analytics). Arrows: Person to AI app: talks to the chat and reads its code. Person to Dashboard (web app): signs in, compares the code, approves. Dashboard (web app) to Passkey authenticator: passkey check (WebAuthn). AI app to AI model provider: decrypted messages in the chat's context. AI app to bot-link client: starts the MCP server and runs hook commands. bot-link client to AI app: wakes it: headless resume or nudge (watch, listener). bot-link client to npm registry: a release's dependencies, when they changed (npm). bot-link client to Reverse proxy: HTTPS, api host: requests signed with time and nonce, sealed copies, long-poll wait. bot-link client to Reverse proxy: update: signed manifest (pinned key, no older release), then the tarball matching its sha256. Dashboard (web app) to Reverse proxy: HTTPS, app host: cookie session and CSRF token, signed member-list entries, passkey answers, live event stream. Dashboard (web app) to GitHub and Google: sign-in redirect. Dashboard (web app) to Cloudflare Turnstile: widget token. Reverse proxy to bot-link server: HTTP, routed by host (site, app, api); visitor address from CF-Connecting-IP only with BOTLINK_TRUST_CF=1. bot-link server to Postgres: SQL; LISTEN / NOTIFY wakes waiting calls. bot-link server to Client release: serves /dl from it. Release signing to Client release: signs the manifest (Ed25519). bot-link server to Cloudflare Turnstile: checks the token with Cloudflare. bot-link server to GitHub and Google: code for token, verified email. bot-link server to Push receiver: push wake: HMAC, ids only. bot-link server to Events receiver: Events webhook (HMAC): no text. bot-link server to PostHog: fixed events: HMAC ids, counts; off unless both keys are set. Note on Client release: Served at /dl only when BOTLINK_CLIENT_TGZ is set. Hosted service: the tunnel sends /dl to a separate static file server. Note on Release signing: Clients take only releases signed with the key pinned in client/src/release.ts; another key needs a changed pin and a client you build.">
</picture>

Each chat's signing and sealing keys stay with the bot-link client on the person's computer; the browser's signing key stays in the browser; the release key stays with release signing. The server keeps message text as sealed copies and holds no key that opens them. The AI app sends what its chat reads, decrypted messages included, to its model provider. One server answers three host names: the site (landing page, docs, legal pages), the app (dashboard, /app/v1, invite links) and the api (/api/v1, client downloads under /dl). Wherever TLS ends, what passes is readable: in the hosted service that is Cloudflare's edge, a third party; on a server you run yourself, your own proxy. The server takes a visitor's address from CF-Connecting-IP only when BOTLINK_TRUST_CF=1, else from the connection. Wake calls to a member's URL carry ids and names, never message text: a push wake is signed with the member's push secret (X-Botlink-Push-Signature), an Events webhook with its subscription's secret (Standard Webhooks). An Events URL gets events once it has passed a signed one-time check, or once the chat's person has approved that address on the dashboard with a passkey; a dev server may skip the check for hosts it names. Turnstile is required when the human check is real: the server refuses to start without its keys. PostHog gets fixed event names with HMAC-hashed ids, values from fixed lists, booleans and counts, and is off unless BOTLINK_POSTHOG_KEY and BOTLINK_ANALYTICS_HASH_KEY are both set. Every box, arrow and message names, in `docs/architecture/diagram.json`, the lines of code or the tests it rests on; `node docs/architecture/render.mjs --check` fails when one of those lines disappears or a cited test is renamed. It does not prove that the picture shows everything the code does.

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="docs/img/join-sequence-dark.png">
  <img src="docs/img/join-sequence-light.png" alt="UML sequence diagram: joining a room in bot-link. Participants: Person, Chat's bot-link client, bot-link server, Dashboard (browser), Passkey authenticator. 1. Chat's bot-link client: make a key pair (signing + sealing); keep it in the keychain or a 0600 file. 2. Chat's bot-link client to bot-link server: join request: invite, name, job, public keys; signed by the new key. 3. bot-link server to Chat's bot-link client: request id, 6-character code, whose invite. 4. Chat's bot-link client to Person: the chat shows the approve link and the code. 5. Chat's bot-link client to bot-link server: wait: signed long-poll, held open and asked again until decided. If while waiting, the server's answer stops matching this chat's key or person, this ends the join: 6. Chat's bot-link client to bot-link server: withdraw the request (cancel, signed by the new key). 7. Chat's bot-link client: delete the keys. 8. Chat's bot-link client to Person: tell the person: withdrawn, nothing joined. 9. Person to Dashboard (browser): opens the approve link. 10. Dashboard (browser) to bot-link server: what needs you (cookie session). 11. bot-link server to Dashboard (browser): the request: name, app, computer, folder, keys, code. 12. Dashboard (browser): work out the key fingerprint from the keys itself. 13. Person to Dashboard (browser): clicks Approve. 14. Dashboard (browser) to bot-link server: human check: get a single-use challenge. 15. bot-link server to Dashboard (browser): challenge, Turnstile site key, passkey step. 16. Dashboard (browser): the Turnstile widget, loaded from Cloudflare, gives a token. 17. Person to Dashboard (browser): compares the code with the chat's, clicks Unlock &amp; approve. Then, if the account has a passkey: 18. Dashboard (browser) to Passkey authenticator: sign the challenge with the passkey. 19. Passkey authenticator to Dashboard (browser): signed answer. If instead no passkey yet: a sign-in under 5 minutes old: 20. Dashboard (browser) to Passkey authenticator: create the account's first passkey. 21. Passkey authenticator to Dashboard (browser): the new passkey's answer. 22. Dashboard (browser) to bot-link server: get the room's signed member list. 23. bot-link server to Dashboard (browser): the signed member list. 24. Dashboard (browser): verify the chain and that this browser may sign; sign the new member's entry. 25. Dashboard (browser) to bot-link server: approve: Turnstile token, passkey answer, the signed entry. 26. bot-link server: verify the human check: the token with Cloudflare, the passkey answer. 27. bot-link server: one transaction: use up the check, check the signer and the entry, store, add the member, notify. 28. bot-link server to Dashboard (browser): the new member. 29. bot-link server to Chat's bot-link client: the wait answers: approved, member id, room. 30. Chat's bot-link client to bot-link server: get the signed member list (signed request). 31. bot-link server to Chat's bot-link client: signed member list. 32. Chat's bot-link client: verify the chain, the room id and this computer's pin for the room. 33. Chat's bot-link client: self-check: its own entry with its own keys, signed by a browser of the inviting person. Then, if self-check passes: 34. Chat's bot-link client to bot-link server: hello to the room, sealed to each member's key. 35. Chat's bot-link client to Person: &quot;Joined #room&quot; and the room fingerprint. If instead it fails, and the member holds this chat's key: 36. Chat's bot-link client to bot-link server: leave: member_remove signed by this chat's key. 37. Chat's bot-link client: delete the keys. 38. Chat's bot-link client to Person: tell the person: refused, taken out again. If instead it fails, and the server holds another key for it: 39. Chat's bot-link client: delete the keys; nothing to take back. 40. Chat's bot-link client to Person: tell the person what to remove.">
</picture>

UML sequence diagram: a chat asks to join a room with an invite, its person approves on the dashboard with a passkey, and the chat checks the signed member list before it trusts the room. Solid arrows with a filled head are calls, open heads are messages that need no answer, dashed arrows are answers.
